item.title: Toroidal-OAM Hybrid Beam for Divergence-Suppressed OAM Wireless Communication
item.description: arXiv:2610.26921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams offer spatially independent multiplexing in wireless communications, but their donut-shaped intensity diverges with mode order, causing power capture loss at finite apertures and unequal link budgets. We propose a toroidal-OAM hybrid beam that combines the angular confinement and strong longitudinal electric field of toroidal electromagnetic pulses from a coaxial horn with a conventional OAM beam, lowering angular spread and producing non-zero on-axis intensity. A far-field model is built as a weighted superposition of OAM uniform circular array (UCA) radiation, a super-Gaussian toroidal angular envelope, and a zeroth-order Bessel longitudinal field, controlled by three dimensionless parameters (toroidal confinement, coupling strength, longitudinal coefficient) tied to measurable hardware. Numerical results at 3 GHz with a $5\lambda$ aperture show 12--41% divergence reduction for OAM modes $\ell = 1$--$4$, while modes $\ell \geq 5$ become fully center-peaked. The suppression ratio stays unchanged for fixed $kR$, $\kappa$, $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\ell$. Link evaluation shows 6.4--30.9 dB received SNR gain, over 108% extension in fixed-efficiency link-budget range, and up to five orders of magnitude reduction in multi-mode power imbalance. The central null is filled to 8--100% of the peak; the hybrid beam does not mix OAM modes, with intended-mode power fraction above $0.54$ where the ring is well-defined. OAM mode-division multiplexing capacity at $z=500\lambda$ shows up to $2.1\times$ ($107\%$) capacity enhancement. Full-wave simulation in ANSYS HFSS corroborates the model, confirming the hybrid launcher preserves the OAM vortex phase while reducing divergence compared with a UCA-only baseline. These findings establish toroidal beam engineering as a practical tool for OAM-based wireless links.
item.dc:creator: Runyu Lyu, Wenchi Cheng, Xiang Fang

item.title: QoS-Aware Joint 1-Bit RIS Element Activation and Fluid-Antenna Port Selection
item.description: arXiv:2610.27291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This letter jointly optimizes fluid-antenna port selection, fixed-cardinality reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) element activation, and 1-bit reflection phases through an exact angular event sweep that extends full-activation divide-and-sort geometry to subset selection. We establish deterministic gain bounds and activation monotonicity, derive exact single-element outage expressions and high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) asymptotics for independent RIS branches with correlated receiving ports, and prove diversity order equal to the RIS element count for fixed positive-definite RIS covariance. With perfect instantaneous channel state information, a quality-of-service aware policy activates the minimum number of elements required to meet a target SNR while preserving full-activation outage probability. An explicit overhead condition identifies when reduced activation improves net energy efficiency. Correlated-channel benchmarks illustrate subset-selection gains, aperture effects, and overhead-dependent energy-efficiency tradeoffs.
item.dc:creator: Khalid Yahya, Mahmoud Aldababsa

item.title: Variational Blind Equalization for Dual-Polarization Free-Space Quantum Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.27358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dual-polarization free-space quantum communication links require receiver equalization under polarization mixing, fading, phase variation, and limited channel supervision. This paper investigates variational blind and semi-blind equalization using VISTA (Variational Inference for Signal Tracking and Adaptation), a variational autoencoder-based probabilistic physical parameter estimator. In the semi-blind branch, channel-relevant statistics are mapped to the underlying 2x2 complex polarization channel. We compare forward KL, reverse KL, Average Jeffreys, Max-KL, and Adaptive Jeffreys regularization and analyze directional KL asymmetry and the local effect of the regularization weight zeta. Over 500 paired Monte Carlo trials, forward KL is nearly insensitive to zeta, whereas reverse and symmetric objectives exhibit low-error regions followed by degradation under stronger regularization. At zeta = 3 x 10^-5, Average Jeffreys reduces median channel NRMSE by approximately 4.8% relative to forward KL at the same weight. Reduced KL asymmetry does not necessarily imply lower channel error. A separate fully blind QPSK receiver estimates a direct equalizer from received data only. Over 3000 paired trials, the VISTA variants have nearly identical median aligned block-NMSE, while their lower mean aligned block-NMSE relative to the CMA-plus-separation baseline is concentrated in difficult, large-error trials. Direct-W optimization with Adam reproduces most of this mean reduction. In the fully blind benchmark, the tested weak regularizers provide no resolved improvement over unregularized VISTA.
item.dc:creator: Anders M. Buvarp, Stefan Werner

item.title: Quaternion-Valued Adaptive Projection Statistics for Neural Receivers in Dual-Polarization Free-Space Quantum Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.27363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dual-polarization free-space quantum communication receivers produce two coupled complex heterodyne streams. We develop robust quaternion receiver methods for such links under fading, polarization mixing, calibration mismatch, impulsive contamination, and other non-Gaussian disturbances. The four polarization and quadrature components are encoded as quaternion-valued samples. We formulate an identifiable effective channel model, Quaternion-Valued Projection Statistics (QVPS), and Adaptive QVPS (AQVPS), which augments samplewise projection outlyingness with robust local second-order descriptors. Robust complex and quaternion channel estimators use radial Huber weighting, while QVPS and AQVPS are evaluated separately as disturbance diagnostics. Neural experiments compare matched real-, complex-, quaternion-, and widely linear complex-valued receivers. Robust estimation reduces sensitivity to non-Gaussian contamination. Local second-order descriptors improve detection of the tested localized disturbances relative to QVPS, and a descriptor-only ablation slightly outperforms full AQVPS. Complex LMMSE gives the lowest evaluation MSE in the clean Gaussian SNR sweep, whereas the Quaternion NN, among the compared receivers with their nominal activations, gives the lowest mean evaluation MSE in the tested contaminated sweeps. Activation-matched experiments indicate that much of the nominal Quaternion NN robustness is attributable to bounded activation rather than quaternion parameterization alone. The methods are evaluated at the receiver processing level and do not constitute a composable CV-QKD security proof.
item.dc:creator: Anders M. Buvarp, Stefan Werner

item.title: Structured PARAFAC Channel Estimation for Flexible Intelligent Metasurface Receivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.27445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flexible intelligent metasurfaces (FIMs) create geometric diversity through aperture morphing, but their configuration-dependent responses complicate uplink channel estimation. This letter considers multiple users sharing a common angular response and develops a structured PARAFAC model across calibrated FIM configurations. Its known identity factor and rank-one pilot-weighted channel factor enable deterministic, noniterative algebraic factor recovery through per-element rank-one approximations, reference-state normalization, global rank-one projection, and a least-squares morphing-factor update. The recovered spatial and morphing factors are then jointly matched to the calibrated manifold to estimate the common angles, user gains, and configuration-dependent channels. Simulations demonstrate accurate recovery and show that out-of-plane morphing resolves the azimuth-sign ambiguity of an undeformed planar aperture; an angular-spread experiment quantifies the mismatch when the common-response assumption is relaxed.
item.dc:creator: Xi Han, Junqiao Chen, Yuansheng Zhang, Andr\'e L. F. de Almeida, George C. Alexandropoulos

item.title: RMSampler: Sparse Radio Map Reconstruction with Active Sampling and Diffusion Posterior Correction
item.description: arXiv:2610.27464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconstructing a radio map (RM) from sparse received-power measurements supports non-cooperative interference monitoring and spectrum management. However,sparse measurements leave uncertainty about both the global RM and the interfering emitter location, making informative sampling and accurate reconstruction challenging. To address these challenges, a novel joint sampling and reconstruction method named RMSampler is proposed in this paper to improve measurement selection and RM reconstruction under limited measurement budgets. For measurement selection, RMSampler evaluates global RM error reduction using the covariance of diffusion-generated RMs and localization error reduction using candidate emitter locations. Because these errors have different units, their expected relative reductions are combined into a scale-invariant sampling criterion, with each acquired measurement updating both uncertainty estimates. After sampling, the updated emitter-location probabilities guide a separate conditional diffusion ensemble for final reconstruction. To improve measurement agreement, an effective sample size (ESS) target guides robust posterior correction, followed by a minimum-distortion projection enforcing measurement and building constraints. For the reconstruction ensemble, analysis establishes that increasing likelihood power reduces expected robust measurement loss, while pretrained neural parameters and architecture remain unchanged. Experiments using simulated and real-world measured data demonstrate improved reconstruction under matched measurement budgets. In the Chongqing real-world measured data experiment, root mean square error (RMSE) decreases from 3.54 to 2.73~dB relative to random sampling under a common reconstruction method.
item.dc:creator: Nan Cheng, Xiucheng Wang

item.title: Multi-Threshold Sampling: Local and Global Parameter Identifiability
item.description: arXiv:2610.27665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-threshold (MT) sampling records threshold-crossing times for parameter estimation in applications including positron emission tomography, oil well logging, and photon-counting X-ray imaging. We study whether the distribution of recorded crossings uniquely determines the signal parameters and how many thresholds are required for this identifiability. For a fixed MT sampler, we show that the ranks of distribution derivatives with respect to the parameters cannot increase through crossing, timing, and selection. Under suitable regularity assumptions, we characterize local identifiability by a full-rank Jacobian of finitely many event probabilities defined on recorded crossings and establish a necessary and sufficient global identifiability criterion under additional rank and topological assumptions. For a nonhomogeneous Poisson signal model with four intensity parameters, a fixed known single-photon response, and deterministic MT sampling, we prove that four cumulative probabilities of the first recorded crossing time establish local and global identifiability under their respective conditions using a single sufficiently small positive threshold. This attains the minimum number of thresholds for the specified model and sampler. Numerical experiments illustrate these results and reveal weak parameter sensitivity and substantial finite-sample estimation errors when estimation uses these probabilities. The results establish parameter uniqueness while highlighting the role of statistical sensitivity in accurate estimation.
item.dc:creator: Ao Qiu, Qingguo Xie

item.title: Revolutionizing 6G Wireless Networks with RISs: Enhancements in Sensing and Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.27695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have emerged as one of the most promising technologies for the next-generation wireless networks, offering advantages such as cost efficiency, low power consumption, flexible deployment, and large effective aperture. Extensive studies have demonstrated the capabilities of RISs to enhance communication performance, including coverage extension, sum-rate improvement, interference suppression, security enhancement, etc. As 6G networks continue to evolve, wireless sensing is expected to play a pivotal role alongside communication. Undoubtedly, RISs possess great potential to enable seamless integration of sensing and communication by supporting both passive and active sensing paradigms. This paper explores how RISs can revolutionize wireless networks by enhancing both communication and sensing capabilities. Specifically, we highlight the fundamental principles, potential applications, and future trends of RIS-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), anticipating that RIS-enabled ISAC will become a key enabler in the upcoming 6G era.
item.dc:creator: Jiguang He, Yuwen Cao, Charles Vanwynsberghe, Aymen Fakhreddine, Yi Fang, Chongwen Huang, George C. Alexandropoulos, Merouane Debbah

item.title: When Every Bit Counts in Quantized Beamforming: From CSI Feedback to Low-Resolution Hardware
item.description: arXiv:2610.27923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) is a key technology in modern wireless networks, but its performance is often analyzed under ideal hardware assumptions. In practical implementations, however, quantization appears throughout the signal-processing chain, including channel state information (CSI) feedback, fronthaul signaling, beamforming coefficients, data converters, and finite-resolution phase shifters. These impairments do not act independently: they alter the channel information available for beamforming, constrain the feasible transmit signals, and can ultimately limit beamforming gain and interference suppression. This article provides a perspective on quantized beamforming by connecting its main sources, performance implications, and mitigation strategies. We discuss codebook-based CSI feedback, quantization-aware beamforming, low-resolution converter modeling, and finite-resolution hybrid beamforming, and use representative numerical examples to illustrate when quantization becomes a dominant performance bottleneck. We further highlight emerging directions in joint beamforming and quantization design, adaptive-resolution architectures, and new antenna technologies with discrete hardware constraints. The key message is that finite-resolution effects should be modeled explicitly and incorporated into the beamforming design rather than treated as an afterthought.
item.dc:creator: Yasaman Khorsandmanesh, Parisa Ramezani, Emil Bjornson

item.title: RIS Configuration with Low-Overhead Measurements via Physics-Guided Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.27972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) configuration for a single-input single-output (SISO) communication link using a two-stage estimate-then-optimize procedure. Within this framework, two common approaches to the estimation stage are pilot-based channel estimation and received signal strength (RSS)-based channel estimation. Our hardware experiments reveal substantial inter-block phase evolution consistent with residual CFO, while simulations show that such phase rotations can severely degrade pilot-based channel estimation when left uncompensated. In contrast, RSS-based approaches are less affected by these phase rotations, although they often require a large number of measurements to achieve a near-optimal received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). To address this measurement requirement, we propose parametric physics-guided neural blind beamforming (\textsc{P-PGNBB}) for RSS-based channel estimation. Simulations and hardware experiments confirm that the proposed method achieves a received SNR close to that obtained with perfect channel state information (CSI) and comparable to existing methods, while requiring substantially fewer RSS measurements.
item.dc:creator: Son Dinh-Van, Matthew D. Higgins

item.title: Diffusion MRI protocol design for reliable parameter recovery: a unified framework across biophysical models
item.description: arXiv:2610.28099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable microstructural parameter estimation in diffusion MRI (dMRI) critically depends on the acquisition protocol. Yet, common protocol design criteria may not fully reflect estimator bias, parameter constraints, and nonlinear fitting behavior in complex inverse problems. Here, we introduce Protocol Optimization via Loss Assessing Parameter Recovery (POLAR), an end-to-end framework that searches the continuous acquisition space and directly minimizes multiparameter recovery error through noisy signal simulation and the chosen model fitting. We demonstrate POLAR spanning distinct microstructural environments: the Cylinder-Zeppelin model for white matter, Neurite Exchange Imaging (NEXI) for gray matter, and Cellular Exchange Imaging (CEXI) for permeable cells. Across independent held-out parameter sets, POLAR consistently outperformed model-specific reference designs, reducing RMSE by up to $50\%$ for Cylinder-Zeppelin and $74\%$ for CEXI, while reducing NEXI exchange time bias by $70\%$. These gains across distinct biophysical models, acquisition settings, and reference design strategies demonstrate the benefit of optimizing acquisition protocols through the downstream parameter-estimation problem. POLAR provides a flexible, model-specific and estimator-aware framework for designing dMRI protocols tailored to the microstructural parameters and experimental conditions of interest.
item.dc:creator: Ekin Taskin, Jonathan Rafael-Pati\~no, Erick Jorge Canales-Rodr\'iguez, Jean-Philippe Thiran

item.title: Negative Log-Shifted Gamma: A Generalized Pointing Error Model for Directional Wideband Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.28101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pointing error is critical in highly directional communication systems, where even slight misalignment leads to severe received power reduction. Existing pointing error models fail to cover diverse practical scenarios due to restrictive distributional and design limitations. This paper proposes a novel pointing error model incorporating jitters, AoD/AoA estimation errors, and comprehensive design impacts, including phase shifter quantization, antenna patterns, array design, beamforming architectures, steering capabilities, and bandwidth. To accomplish this, antenna patterns are modeled for both high- and low-gain configurations. Then, the array factor's main lobe is approximated as a Gaussian beam for subarrays and superarrays, accommodating analog and digital beamforming stages in wideband systems under beam squint presence or compensation. Jitters and estimation errors are incorporated via 3D rotations, while phase shift quantization is captured through the phase excitations of the arrays. It is shown that the resulting pointing error follows a novel distribution: the negative log-shifted Gamma (NLSG). Fully characterized by only shape, scale, and location parameters, the NLSG features closed-form statistical expressions. This formulation ensures tractable mathematical manipulation, making it a practical, scalable tool for system design and analysis. Validation via normalized moment error, Jensen-Shannon divergence, and Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics confirms exceptional accuracy, yielding values primarily below 1%, 0.02, and 0.05, respectively. Furthermore, capacity analysis has demonstrated that specific design choices are paramount for achieving optimal capacity. Finally, important guidelines for designing highly directional wideband communication systems are provided to mitigate the detrimental effects of pointing errors, thereby paving the way for robust next-generation networks.
item.dc:creator: Evla S. Ahrazoglu, Ahmet C. Gul, Mehmet N. Akinci, Ibrahim Altunbas, Eylem Erdogan

item.title: Interference-Graph-Aided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Beam Hopping LEO Satellite Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.28248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beam hopping technology enables LEO satellites to dynamically switch beam coverage positions, providing flexible resource allocation for non-uniformly distributed traffic demands. However, the severe spatial interference coupling among beams makes coordinated scheduling challenging. To address this problem, in this letter, we propose an interference-graph-aided multi-agent reinforcement learning approach that constructs an interference graph to capture beam coupling relationships and injects this structural prior into agent-side representation learning. Each beam agent aggregates information from interference neighbors via graph convolution before estimating local Q-values, which are then decomposed by the standard mixing network. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 34.4\% higher throughput than QMIX with more stable interference management, under non-uniform traffic and co-channel interference settings.
item.dc:creator: Hao Yuan, Ziyi Yang, Xing Zhang

item.title: Uncertainty-Aware Distributed Radio Map Estimation in Decentralized Wireless Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.28293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning based radio map estimation (RME) approaches rely on frequent exchange of high-dimensional model updates and often require a central server for collaboration coordination and update aggregation. This incurs prohibitively high communication overhead, rendering them impractical for bandwidth-constrained mobile and wireless edge networks. Moreover, in practical mobile sensing scenarios, sparse and unevenly collected measurements lead to estimation uncertainty, which is critical for guiding RME and collaboration among distributed nodes. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an uncertainty-aware distributed radio map estimation (UA-D-RME) framework for decentralized networks. In UA-D-RME, each node locally infers a probabilistic model from its sparse measurements to estimate both its local radio map and the associated estimation uncertainty. Instead of exchanging raw data or model updates, neighboring nodes communicate only low-dimensional statistical information, including radio map and uncertainty measures over their overlapping monitoring areas. An uncertainty-aware statistical consensus mechanism is then developed to iteratively align probabilistic models in neighborhood by ensuring consistency on estimation confidence. Theoretical analysis establishes the convergence of the proposed consensus mechanism and characterizes the distributed generalization performance of the proposed UA-D-RME method. Experiments on urban radio map datasets verify that UA-D-RME achieves desired reconstruction accuracy comparable to the centralized RME benchmark while reducing communication costs and without exchanging raw measurements.
item.dc:creator: Dong Yang, Zhuoyu Yao, Yue Wang, Songyang Zhang, Yingshu Li, Zhi Tian, Zhipeng Cai

item.title: Stabilizing Filters for Graph Signal Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.28318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating graph signals is an important task in machine learning, and incorporating the underlying graph into a generative model enables structurally-informed distribution modeling. However, said graph is often noisy or imperfectly estimated, and structural errors can affect the generative process and the resulting signal distribution. While recent work has established stability guarantees for graph neural ordinary differential equations, the robustness of graph-aware reference dynamics, as used in topological Schr\"odinger bridge models, remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the structural stability of continuous-time generative models whose dynamics combine a graph filter with a learned graph neural network. We first derive a Wasserstein stability bound that quantifies the effect of graph perturbations on the generated signal distributions. Informed by this analysis, we then propose a principled framework for designing graph filters that balance structural stability with induced signal smoothing. We characterize the optimal filter design and provide an explicit family of polynomial filters with provable stability guarantees. Experiments on synthetic graphs and real-world fMRI signals support our theoretical findings, illustrating the enhanced structural stability of the proposed filters while preserving generative performance.
item.dc:creator: Martin Schmidt, Gonzalo Mateos

item.title: Finite-Size CV-QKD for Satellite Quantum Communication under a Hybrid Noise Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.28353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Satellite-based continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is fundamentally constrained by finite communication windows, channel attenuation, and statistical fluctuations arising from a limited number of exchanged quantum states. This work develops a finite-size CV-QKD framework for satellite quantum communication under a hybrid noise model that jointly incorporates satellite geometry, atmospheric and propagation losses, quantum Poissonian noise coexisting with classical additive white Gaussian noise, detector imperfections, and composable finite-key security under collective attacks. A single canonical finite-size secret key rate (SKR) expression is derived in which the finite-size correction is stated in a strictly decreasing form in the block size, removing the ambiguity between the segmented and the block-level formulations used in earlier treatments. The finite-size accounting is further extended to the quantum bit error ratio (QBER) through an explicit parameter estimation penalty, so that the feasibility constraint inherits the same block-size dependence as the key rate. The framework quantifies the influence of reconciliation efficiency, transmission efficiency, detection efficiency, receiver aperture, beam waist, zenith angle, wavelength, and effective communication time. Numerical results reveal a significant performance gap between finite-size and asymptotic operation, indicating that asymptotic analysis can overestimate the feasible satellite altitude by a factor of several, and that the achievable range is governed by the number of signals actually exchanged rather than by any single physical channel parameter. These results establish block size as a first-class design variable for satellite CV-QKD mission dimensioning.
item.dc:creator: Mouli Chakraborty, Avishek Nag, Subhash Chandra, Anshu Mukherjee, Konstantinos Koufos, Mehrdad Dianati

item.title: Topology-Adaptive Seismic Response Prediction of Interconnected Structural Systems Using Reduced Order Model Embedded Graph Neural Network
item.description: arXiv:2610.28378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrical substation equipment is commonly interconnected by busbars and flexible conductors. Such interconnected infrastructures exhibit complex dynamic interactions, where the response of each component is influenced by local structural properties, mechanical coupling, system topology, and transient excitation. High-fidelity FE models can capture some of these effects, but their computational cost limits their use for real-time prediction. Purely data-driven models offer faster inference, yet they struggle to generalize, requiring additional simulations and retraining for each new configuration. This work presents a ROM embedded Graph Neural Network (ROMeGNN) for topology-aware seismic digital twins of interconnected structural systems. The system is represented as a graph, where structural components are treated as nodes and mechanical interconnections as edges. Each high-fidelity component model is first reduced to a reduced-order modal representation, which forms a differentiable dynamics operator within the GNN. Rather than learning the full response directly, the GNN estimates topology-dependent interaction forces that enter the differentiable ROM solver as coupling inputs for modal state advancement. This hybrid formulation preserves the known component-level physics and uses data-driven message passing to learn complex inter-component forces across varying system layouts. The framework is demonstrated on interconnected electrical substation equipment subjected to randomized seismic inputs. It delivers rapid predictions of response quantities relevant to seismic damage assessment while remaining applicable across varying layouts, component combinations, and excitation scenarios. These results highlight the potential of embedding physics within graph learning architectures for real-time, interpretable, topology-adaptive seismic digital twins of interconnected engineering systems.
item.dc:creator: Huangbin Liang, Beatriz Moya, Francisco Chinesta, Eleni Chatzi

item.title: ORCA: Onboard Reflective Collaborative Agents for Reliable Task Offloading in LEO Satellite Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.28404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites increasingly perform time-critical onboard processing, yet heterogeneous computing capabilities, rapidly changing inter-satellite links (ISLs) and uncertain neighbor behavior make decentralized task offloading difficult under partial observations. This paper presents ORCA, an architecture of Onboard Reflective Collaborative Agents for autonomous onboard task offloading. ORCA organizes offloading decisions into a four-Agent \emph{Perceive}$\rightarrow$\emph{Reason}$\rightarrow$ \emph{Act}$\rightarrow$\emph{Learn} loop. It aims to improve efficiency and reliability in dynamic, heterogeneous, and unreliable LEO satellite networks. The simulation results of a heterogeneous 60-satellite Walker-delta constellation demonstrates that ORCA delivers competitive system efficiency in cooperative settings while achieving superior task-success robustness and offloading reliability under previously unseen malicious node behavior, indicating that outcome-grounded reflection can improve the reliability of decentralized onboard offloading without centralized runtime coordination.
item.dc:creator: Yunxin Geng, Shengxiang Hao, Yichen Wu, Haotian Liu, Weiwei Jiang, Lu Cao, Han Meng, Yuxuan Pan, Zhiqing Wei

item.title: How Much of Cross-Subject EEG Emotion Recognition Is Stimulus Memorization?
item.description: arXiv:2610.28422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-subject EEG emotion recognition now reports accuracies above 90% on stimulus-defined benchmarks such as SEED, and the field has examined several ways in which such numbers can be inflated, attributing inflation to subject identity, to data partitioning, and to repeated stimulus presentation. We observe that one variable has been left out. On these datasets the emotion label is assigned to the video at design time, so any encoder that recovers which video was shown obtains the label for free. We adapt three representation-level shortcut diagnostics to a cohort of published contrastive cross-subject encoders, and find that stimulus identity is linearly recoverable at six to fifteen times chance. We then measure its impact on the reported accuracy by holding out subjects and stimuli jointly, and find that each released classifier loses two to forty-four points once the test videos are unseen, so a headline obtained under subject hold-out alone is not a measure of cross-subject emotion decoding.
item.dc:creator: Haiyan Xu, Konstantinos N. Plataniotis

item.title: A Hierarchical Space-Ground Collaborative Network: Architecture Design and Deployment
item.description: arXiv:2610.28459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The sixth-generation (6G) landscape demands a profound architectural evolution toward a unified, collaborative ecosystem that integrates satellite and terrestrial segments to provide ubiquitous global connectivity. Nevertheless, conventional independent management paradigms are increasingly challenged by the profound spatiotemporal nonstationarity of low-Earth orbit (LEO) channels and the volatile demands of massive heterogeneous services. To address these challenges, this study focuses on the architectural design of space-ground integrated networks (SGINs) and investigates elastic deployment strategies tailored to heterogeneous 6G service requirements. We first review the development trends in SGIN and then summarize typical application scenarios into two categories, along with their associated challenges and constraints. After that, a hierarchical space-ground collaborative network (SGCN) architecture is proposed to support achieving larger network capability, extensive continuous coverage, and enhanced spectral efficiency, which is evaluated through three representative scenarios with progressive baselines. Subsequently, a service-aware deployment strategy is introduced to further establish the engineering feasibility of the proposed architecture.
item.dc:creator: Yunxin Geng, Shaopeng Feng, Zijian Guo, Shengfeng Wang, Rui Ding, Kan Zheng, Zhiqing Wei, Weiwei Jiang, Zhiyong Feng

item.title: Delayed Convergence of S-Parameter Sensitivities to Design Parameters in FDTD Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, the sensitivities of S-parameters to design parameters come from discrete Fourier transforms of responses ending at a simulation time T. We show that, when a design parameter moves a resonance, the sensitivity converges later than the S-parameter. For a single mode with field decay time $\tau$, the truncation error of the sensitivity is $(1+T/\tau)e^{-T/\tau}$, against $e^{-T/\tau}$ for the resonant part of the S-parameter, so a 1% sensitivity error needs $T \geq 6.6\tau$ instead of $4.6\tau$. Automatic differentiation, the discrete adjoint and finite differences on the same run carry this error, so their agreement cannot reveal it. In three solvers, with no fitted parameter, the estimate predicts the simulated error within 4% at cavity resonances with $Q$ of 1000-7000; at lower $Q$ the error is larger. On a cavity whose slowest mode is weakly coupled, common end criteria leave $|S_{11}|$ within 0.5 dB of a 1.3 dB dip but its sensitivity 10-72% in error. A matrix-pencil extrapolation inside the differentiable computation recovers the sensitivity on a cavity with field probes from a run 66 times shorter. In a single-pole filter loop with a symmetric objective, truncation leaves the maximum of the objective in place, and the optimizer reaches the resonance of a full run despite the wrong gradient. With two coupled poles, the truncated objective moves the optimum: on runs of $1\tau$ it over-couples by $\Delta k \approx 1.24/Q$, and an equal-ripple objective still shifts it by about $0.2\bar{\alpha}$ at $3\tau$, but not at $4.6\tau$.
item.dc:creator: Byungkwan Kim

item.title: Beamfocusing Versus Airy Beams: Does Antenna Blockage Require Beam Bending?
item.description: arXiv:2610.28557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Airy beams are often proposed in array beamforming to bend beams around obstacles. We prove that, for a single-antenna receiver, conventional beamfocusing maximizes the received power regardless of how many antennas are blocked and, in expectation, even with phase errors in the channel state information. This also holds for multi-antenna receivers under a phase-separability condition that is satisfied in rank-one channels. Numerical results confirm that unmodified beamfocusing is optimal for physically small receivers (i.e., those that fit within the beamwidth) when an obstacle is present. For physically larger receivers, the optimal precoding deviates from beamfocusing to better illuminate the receiver's unobstructed parts, but will not become Airy beams. While Airy beams can be configured to perform well, their ability to follow a bent trajectory in front of an obstacle does not maximize the received power behind it.
item.dc:creator: Emil Bj\"ornson, Vitaly Petrov, Erik G. Larsson

item.title: Exploring Representation Autoencoders for Text-to-Audio Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Representation autoencoders (RAE), created by pairing a frozen pretrained self-supervised learning (SSL) encoder with a trained decoder, have recently demonstrated state-of-the-art performance on image generation. Their use in the audio domain, however, remains limited: text-to-audio (TTA) models are typically trained in the latent space of dedicated autoencoders where the encoder and the decoder are trained jointly with reconstruction objectives. This paper presents a study on audio representation autoencoders (AuRA) and their applicability to general audio TTA. We train decoders for two pretrained SSL audio encoders and evaluate their reconstruction quality against autoencoders used by recent TTA systems. After obtaining decoders for the SSL representations, we also train rectified flow models in the SSL and baseline latent spaces to isolate the autoencoder's effect on generation. We find that generation in SSL spaces achieves comparable or superior performance to generation in the baseline spaces, despite differences in reconstruction performance. These results highlight that reconstruction quality alone is not a sufficient proxy for generative performance.
item.dc:creator: Bernardo V. Miranda (S2A, IDS), Hugo Malard (S2A, IDS), Ga\"el Richard (S2A, IDS), Mathieu Fontaine (LTCI, IP Paris), Slim Essid (IDS, S2A, LTCI)

item.title: Sionna Bench: Towards Benchmarks in Wireless Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.27174v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Academic research in wireless communications has no tradition of benchmarks so far. Remarkable progress in benchmark-oriented fields like machine learning suggests that the adoption of benchmarks could benefit our field. In the absence of benchmarks, however, a scientific debt has accumulated: since the academic community has not canonized specific problem setups, methods that address essentially the same problem were often developed for slightly different setups and lack a common framework for comparison. Any attempt to establish a new benchmark is faced with the challenge of resolving this debt. Recent advances in agentic artificial intelligence (AI) create an opportunity to do so by leveraging AI-assisted coding. This makes it possible to implement the state-of-the art at scale and to adapt it to a common framework for comparison. We present Sionna Bench to initiate benchmarks in academic wireless communications research. As a pilot study, we use the problem of MIMO-OFDM channel estimation. At the time of writing, Sionna Bench's channel estimation benchmark features twenty channel estimation methods that were implemented from ten different papers. The ability to compare methods against the state-of-the-art will be crucial for navigating the research landscape in an era where AI-generated methods coexist with human-developed algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Gian Marti, Jakob Hoydis, Fay\c{c}al A\"it Aoudia, Sebastian Cammerer, Alexander Keller

item.title: Toward Agentic AI for the 6G Physical Layer: From Algorithm Discovery to Verified Baseband Silicon
item.description: arXiv:2610.27797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: 6G will be designed faster than it can be built: AI-driven search already proposes physical-layer algorithms at machine speed, while carrying a single one onto embedded baseband silicon remains specialist work. That silicon imposes hard memory and numeric limits, but also exposes cost structures a GPU lacks, and a design flow that never runs on the target sees neither. We present an agentic workflow in which an LLM coding agent implements algorithms on a commercial baseband SoC, optimizes them down to agent-written vector assembly, and validates them on silicon. The agent is guided by a knowledge base of measured platform facts, checked at every step against evaluators it is instructed never to edit, and metered per phase. We showcase the workflow on an AI-discovered orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) detector portfolio on the open 6G4All platform. It yields twelve kernels that run cycle-exactly on silicon, their optimized versions at 18k-405k cycles (30-660 $\mu$s) per frame. It also yields a new detector shaped by the chip's measured costs that needs 13.9% fewer cycles than the port of the discovered detector while matching its error rate, with a measured edge our evaluation cannot statistically resolve, a structure that a hardware-blind search objective had no reason to find. What is not specific to OTFS is the workflow: an LLM agent exploring an implementation space under real hardware limits, with the cost of every choice measured rather than assumed.
item.dc:creator: Eric Mittag, Lukas Brechtel, Maximilian Stark, Hans D. Schotten

item.title: Respiro: Continuous Respiratory Rate Monitoring During Motion via Wearable Ultra-Wideband Radar
item.description: arXiv:2411.08898v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deviations in respiratory rate often precede abnormalities in other vital signs. However, continuously monitoring respiratory rates outside clinical settings remains challenging due to the obtrusive nature and sensitivity to body motions in existing monitoring approaches. In this study, we propose a single-point-of-contact wearable device that leverages off-the-shelf, consumer-grade ultra-wideband radar to monitor respiratory rate as part of a chest strap. Our signal processing pipeline reliably extracts the wearer's respiratory signal from windowed complex channel impulse responses. In a controlled experiment, twelve participants performed various activities to evaluate the system's accuracy under motion while capturing ground-truth recordings through a spirometer. Our method extracted respiratory rates with less than 1 breath per minute deviation in 71% of all measurements, averaging 1.11 breaths per minute across all sessions and participants. Our findings underscore the potential of consumer-grade ultra-wideband radar technology in body-worn devices for unobtrusive yet effective respiratory monitoring.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Reidy, Manuel Meier, Christian Holz

item.title: Robust Heart Rate Detection via Multi-Site Photoplethysmography
item.description: arXiv:2412.17538v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Smartwatches have become popular for monitoring physiological parameters outside clinical settings. Using reflective photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors, such watches can non-invasively estimate heart rate (HR) in everyday environments and throughout a patient's day. However, achieving consistently high accuracy remains challenging, particularly during moments of increased motion or due to varying device placement. In this paper, we introduce a novel sensor fusion method for estimating HR that flexibly combines samples from multiple PPG sensors placed across the patient's body, including wrist, ankle, head, and sternum (chest). Our method first estimates signal quality across all inputs to dynamically integrate them into a joint and robust PPG signal for HR estimation. We evaluate our method on a novel dataset of PPG and ECG recordings from 14 participants who engaged in real-world activities outside the laboratory over the course of a whole day. Our method achieves a mean HR error of 2.4\,bpm, which is 46\% lower than the mean error of the best-performing single device (4.4\,bpm, head).
item.dc:creator: Manuel Meier, Christian Holz

item.title: Tri-Spectral PPG: Robust Reflective Photoplethysmography by Fusing Multiple Wavelengths for Cardiac Monitoring
item.description: arXiv:2412.17549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-channel photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors have found widespread adoption in wearable devices for monitoring cardiac health. Channels thereby serve different functions -- whereas green is commonly used for metrics such as heart rate and heart rate variability, red and infrared are commonly used for pulse oximetry. In this paper, we introduce a novel method that simultaneously fuses multi-channel PPG signals into a single recovered PPG signal that can be input to further processing. Via signal fusion, our learning-based method compensates for the artifacts that affect wavelengths to different extents, such as motion and ambient light changes. We evaluate our method on a novel dataset of multi-channel PPG recordings and electrocardiogram recordings for reference from 10 participants over the course of 13 hours during real-world activities outside the laboratory. Using the fusion PPG signal our method recovered, participants' heart rates can be calculated with a mean error of 4.5\,bpm (23\% lower than from green PPG signals at 5.9\,bpm).
item.dc:creator: Manuel Meier, Berken Utku Demirel, Christian Holz

item.title: BMAR: Barometric and Motion-based Alignment and Refinement for Offline Signal Synchronization across Devices
item.description: arXiv:2501.16015v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A requirement of cross-modal signal processing is accurate signal alignment. Though simple on a single device, accurate signal synchronization becomes challenging as soon as multiple devices are involved, such as during activity monitoring, health tracking, or motion capture - particularly outside controlled scenarios where data collection must be standalone, low-power, and support long runtimes. In this paper, we present BMAR, a novel synchronization method that operates purely based on recorded signals and is thus suitable for offline processing. BMAR needs no wireless communication between devices during runtime and does not require any specific user input, action, or behavior. BMAR operates on the data from devices worn by the same person that record barometric pressure and acceleration - inexpensive, low-power, and thus commonly included sensors in today's wearable devices. In its first stage, BMAR verifies that two recordings were acquired simultaneously and pre-aligns all data traces. In a second stage, BMAR refines the alignment using acceleration measurements while accounting for clock skew between devices. In our evaluation, three to five body-worn devices recorded signals from the wearer for up to ten hours during a series of activities. BMAR synchronized all signal recordings with a median error of 33.4 ms and reliably rejected non-overlapping signal traces. The worst-case activity was sleeping, where BMAR's second stage could not exploit motion for refinement and, thus, aligned traces with a median error of 3.06 s.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Meier, Christian Holz

item.title: Handover-Aware Power Minimization for Networked LEO Satellite Communications: Joint Cooperative Beamforming and Scheduling
item.description: arXiv:2603.07434v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Networked low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations enabled by inter-satellite links offer a promising path toward ubiquitous broadband non-terrestrial services, as cooperative transmission increases the received power and suppresses interference. However, fast orbital motion induces frequent handovers, which cost energy and transmission time, while the limited number of radio-frequency chains per satellite couples user scheduling with cooperative beamforming. In this paper, we investigate handover-aware power-efficient downlink transmission in networked LEO systems under statistical channel state information. Specifically, we first introduce a two-segment frame structure that separates the handover procedure from user-plane transmission, and propose a power consumption model that captures the energy to establish each new satellite-user link and the transmission time lost during its handover. We then formulate a per-frame network-wide power minimization problem that jointly optimizes cooperative beamforming and user scheduling, and develop an iterative algorithm that combines a reweighted $\ell_2$ surrogate with a penalty-based relaxation and a fractional-programming inner loop, which yields convex subproblems. Simulation results with Red Sea ship traffic demonstrate that, at $25$~Mbps per user, the proposed design needs 14\% less power than distance-based cooperative scheduling and 15\% less than a joint design that ignores the established links, while non-cooperative transmission meets the rate requirements in only 14\% of the frames.
item.dc:creator: Yuchen Zhang, Eva Lagunas, Symeon Chatzinotas, Tareq Y. Al-Naffouri

item.title: Sparse Solution Trade-offs in GMP DPD: A Least Squares Thresholding Approach
item.description: arXiv:2606.14907v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Power amplifiers (PAs) in satellite communication systems introduce nonlinear distortion, degrading spectral fidelity. Digital pre-distortion linearizes the PA response, but full-complexity solutions are prohibitive under strict size, weight, and power (SWaP) constraints. We propose the use of Least Squares Thresholding (LST) and compare it against Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) and Matching Pursuit. LST achieves a 2.77x complexity reduction while maintaining near-identical linearization performance to OMP.
item.dc:creator: Ellison Murray

item.title: Evolving Intelligent Complex Systems via Intellicise Networks: Architecture, Technologies, and Pathways
item.description: arXiv:2607.00316v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Future engineering infrastructures are evolving into large-scale, open, heterogeneous, and wirelessly interconnected complex systems. These systems present significant challenges in optimizing network resource utilization, managing high-dimensional information spaces, and accommodating diverse business requirements. Intellicise networks, characterized by Intent-driven operation, semantic-native capability, and distributed intelligence, offer a promising paradigm for enabling such intelligent complex systems. We provide a systematic exploration of future intelligent complex systems from the perspective of intellicise networks. Specifically, we propose a cross-domain intelligent communication network architecture based on intellicise networks, grounded in information theory, systems theory, game theory, and cybernetics. The architecture comprises a cross-layer organizational framework, multi-functional planes, and novel information flows. The cross-layer framework defines the vertical evolution from perception and cognition to decision, while the control, user, data, computation, intelligence, and security planes deliver horizontal intellicise capabilities. Moreover, data, knowledge, model, and task flows interconnect the various layers and planes, forming a closed-loop process that derives simplicity from high-level intelligene while concurrently pursuing enhanced. Building on this architecture, we review key enabling technologies, tracing their evolution from semantic extraction to intent understanding, from heterogeneous resource integration to self-configuration and self-optimization, from generative artificial intelligence (AI) to agentic AI, and from embodied AI to symbodied AI. Additionally, we present a case study on intellicise networks for embodied agent communications and discuss representative applications and services for intelligent complex systems.
item.dc:creator: Ping Zhang, Rui Meng, Xiaodong Xu, Song Gao, Zixuan Huang, Yaheng Wang, Yinqiu Liu, Ruichen Zhang, Yiming Liu, Kaiwen Yu, Yaping Sun, Han Meng, Haonan Tong, Huishi Song, Qianqian Yang, Shuoyao Wang, Lexi Xu, Qinghe Du, Geng Sun, Jiawen Kang, Gang Wu, Yiqing Zhou, Haixia Zhang, Zesong Fei, Aimin Hao, Ming Li

item.title: Beam-Domain Channel Estimation for mmWave MIMO using Sub-6 GHz Out-of-Band Information
item.description: arXiv:2607.24227v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Future wireless multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems will integrate sub-6 GHz and millimeter wave (mmWave) bands to support high data rates for latency-critical applications. The coexistence of these bands enables the use of reliable out-of-band sub-6 GHz information to assist mmWave link establishment, particularly for channel estimation. In this paper, we propose a novel beam-domain channel estimation method for mmWave MIMO that leverages sub-6 GHz beam-domain information to improve estimation accuracy. We compare the proposed method with conventional in-band methods. Simulation results show that our proposed method outperform existing baselines in terms of spectral efficiency, in both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) scenarios.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 2026 International Symposium on Wireless Communication Systems (ISWCS), 2026
item.dc:creator: Faruk Pasic, Mariam Mussbah, Stefan Schwarz, Markus Rupp

item.title: Reliability- and Connectivity-Constrained Age-of-Information Optimization for UAV Swarm IoT Data Collection
item.description: arXiv:2608.00061v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle~(UAV) swarms provide a flexible platform for Internet of Things~(IoT) data collection by gathering delay-sensitive measurements from distributed sensor clusters and relaying them to a fusion center~(FC). Between successive updates, the FC estimates the current value of each monitored quantity; however, the estimation accuracy degrades as the last update ages. Such missions require jointly optimizing estimation accuracy, short-packet communication reliability, and swarm connectivity, yet existing approaches typically prioritize freshness while neglecting its impact on connectivity. This paper proposes a topology-coupled urgency~(TCU) scheduler that minimizes the FC's accumulated estimation error while incorporating the swarm's expected algebraic connectivity into the scheduling objective. The resulting connectivity reward encourages idle UAVs to reposition so as to preserve swarm connectivity. For each time slot, the resulting problem is a mixed-integer nonconvex program, which we solve by successive convex approximation. Specifically, the binary assignments are relaxed, while the connectivity reward is represented through a linear matrix inequality on the expected Laplacian. The finite-blocklength rate and the inter-UAV link reliability are linearized in the same convex subproblem, thereby preserving their coupling rather than separating them into alternating blocks. The integer assignments are subsequently recovered by Hungarian matching and verified against the original nonconvex constraints, while a deficit mechanism ensures long-term cluster coverage without requiring explicit long-horizon planning. In simulations comprising more than $19{,}000$ transmission attempts, all delivered updates satisfy the reliability target...
item.dc:creator: Milad Bafarassat, Sinem Coleri

item.title: Robust Model Order Selection via Dithered Differential Step-Down Thresholding
item.description: arXiv:2608.29868v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a differential step-down thresholding algorithm with randomized grid dithering for robust model order selection. It detects the value clustering of noise extrema. Our algorithm asymptotically achieves exact order recovery and prevents false alarms even under lowered detection thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandr Kharin

item.title: ECGWmark: Deep Watermarking of Electrocardiogram Signals With Error-Correcting Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.13357v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings pass through multiple networks and systems before automated interpretation, making patient metadata vulnerable to loss. Digital watermarking embeds this metadata directly into the signal. However, conventional ECG watermarking methods fail under temporal desynchronization, and waveform similarity does not guarantee downstream diagnostic preservation. This article presents ECGWmark, a deep watermarking framework for single-lead ECG. A fully convolutional generator embeds the payload without signal quantization, a detector decodes the message frame by frame and verifies watermark presence, and a frozen arrhythmia classifier penalizes changes that would alter diagnostic predictions. To bridge the gap between bit accuracy and whole-message recovery, payloads are protected by extended Hamming codes, validation-selected interleaving, and soft-decision decoding. On the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, ECGWmark maintains over 90\% bit accuracy under time shifts of 10 to 50 samples, where transform baselines fall to chance level. With the coding layer, the protected 16-bit payload achieves 99.86\% exact recovery on clean segments and sustains over 90\% recovery under time shifts, 10\% sample deletion, and 10\% packet loss. Inter-patient evaluation confirms improved ventricular-beat sensitivity with preserved macro-F1. Requiring only 0.56 million parameters and about 15~ms per segment on a desktop CPU, ECGWmark highlights the need to assess physiological watermarking through whole-message recovery and diagnostic consistency.
item.dc:creator: Kuan-Yu Chen, Kuan-Chen Wang, Yu Tsao, Jian-Jiun Ding

item.title: A Deep Zero-Inflated Model of North Atlantic Right Whale Presence To Support Blue Economy Management
item.description: arXiv:2606.14403v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Effective modeling of endangered marine mammal species, such as the North Atlantic Right Whale, is critical for balancing marine conservation with the growing blue economy. Passive acoustic monitoring data collected by autonomous underwater vehicles provide new opportunities for localized marine species detection and oceanographic sensing, but introduce complex statistical challenges such as zero inflation, imperfect detection, and intricate dependence structures. In response, we propose the Deep Zero-Inflated Bernoulli (DeepZIB) model, a deep statistical method which jointly models latent species presence and conditional detection probabilities while learning complex habitat relationships from heterogeneous covariate information. We establish theoretical results on the model's structural properties and conduct simulation experiments to demonstrate its ability to recover underlying parameters and latent presence fields. Application to real-world passive acoustic monitoring data on the North Atlantic Right Whale along the U.S. East Coast demonstrates improved model adequacy and predictive performance in capturing the species' dynamic and spatially varying habitat. We demonstrate DeepZIB's ability to generate high-resolution, spatially and temporally varying presence maps, providing valuable insights for targeted and risk-aware management of blue economy industries, ranging from offshore and marine energy, to fisheries management and maritime transport
item.dc:creator: Jiaxiang Ji, Laura Nazzaro, Ahmed Aziz Ezzat

item.title: DiffEEG: A Self-Supervised Denoising Diffusion Model for Learning EEG seizure-related Representations
item.description: arXiv:2607.11578v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep learning for EEG-based seizure detection faces critical challenges: severe annotation scarcity and extreme class imbalance, where ictal events comprise less than 10\% of clinical recordings. We present DiffEEG, a 9.6M-parameter self-supervised foundation model that addresses both limitations through denoising diffusion pre-training and reinforcement learning (RL)-based fine-tuning. Pre-trained on 1.3M unlabeled segments from the Temple University Hospital Seizure Corpus (TUHSZ), DiffEEG learns generic neural representations via a 1D U-Net with multi-head self-attention. For downstream adaptation, a reinforced decision layer employs policy gradient optimization to directly maximize F1-score, prioritizing sensitivity to rare seizure events over overall accuracy. Under strict patient-wise evaluation (279 patients, Leave-One-Fold-Out), DiffEEG achieves 61\% accuracy and 59\% F1 for 4-class seizure subtyping, and 81\% accuracy with 85\% weighted F1 for binary detection, maintaining clinically viable seizure recall (59\%) despite extreme imbalance (6.7\% prevalence). Segment-level evaluation establishes an upper bound of 97.6\% accuracy, confirming strong architectural capacity. DiffEEG demonstrates that diffusion-based pre-training combined with metric-aware reinforcement learning enables clinically deployable seizure monitoring with minimal labeled data requirements.
item.dc:creator: Abdulkader Helwan, Lina Abou-Abbas, Hussein El Amouri, Belkacem Chikhaoui, Khadidja Henni
